completion_data.completion_summary: Implemented Phase 1 of 5: sapience-project-bind.sh gained a mode selector (create/bind/pick), a fetch_project_rows() helper correctly filtering (.shared // []) + (.received // []) by accepted-or-owner, a pick-mode listing, and case-insensitive --project resolution to exactly one row, with no write or POST performed. Added test cases 15-17 and a GET /v1/people/projects stub branch; all 17 cases (36 assertions) pass against the source store.

memory_candidates.content: When a plan phase edits a file under agent-system/extensions/** and its test suite uses common_test_resolve_subject with mode "deploy-tree-first", the in-phase verification MUST export CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store or it silently runs the STALE deployed .claude/ copy instead of the edited source. common_test_resolve_subject emits only a stderr WARNING in that case and still returns the deployed path, never a non-zero exit -- so a phase whose verification criteria just name the suite will pass green against unedited code. The alternative (running deploy-headless.sh inside the phase) is a whole-tree claim that serializes against every concurrent sibling, so the env override is the right choice for a per-phase check and the redeploy belongs at the orchestration close.

bash .claude/scripts/verify-touched.sh runs run-all.sh in DEPLOYED mode by default (scripts root .claude/scripts), which ignores CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE entirely and so silently exercises a stale .claude/scripts mirror instead of edited agent-system/extensions/** source, even when the exact same suite also passes correctly when invoked directly with CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store. A phase whose only in-phase check is the bare verify-touched.sh invocation can pass green without ever running the edited code; the direct source-store invocation of the named test suite is the authoritative check, and verify-touched.sh's green result should be treated as a non-informative confirmation of suite wiring, not of the edit's correctness, until the deployed mirror is refreshed.

sapience_notes.subject: GET /v1/people/projects response shape
sapience_notes.value: The real response is {ok, candidates, shared, received, invites, ...} -- never {projects: [...]} and never a bare array. The caller's accepted-or-owned row set is (.shared // []) + (.received // []) | map(select(.accepted or .owner)). The has("projects")/bare-array idiom used elsewhere in this extension resolves to [] against this real shape.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-touched.sh and the deployed-mirror staleness hazard
sapience_notes.value: bash .claude/scripts/verify-touched.sh invokes run-all.sh in deployed mode by default and does not forward or respect CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE, so it silently tests the stale .claude/scripts mirror rather than edited agent-system/extensions/** source. A green verify-touched.sh result is not evidence the edited code was exercised; the authoritative per-phase check for a source-store edit is the direct CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store invocation of the named suite.

sapience_notes.subject: shellcheck SC2034 and multiple assignments
sapience_notes.value: shellcheck's SC2034 (appears unused) flags the LAST assignment site of a variable it considers unused, not the first. A `# shellcheck disable=SC2034` comment placed above an earlier declaration (e.g. FORCE="") does not suppress a later re-assignment of the same variable inside a case arm; the disable comment must sit directly above the assignment shellcheck actually flags.

sapience_notes.subject: Mode-selector design preserving pre-existing CLI test behavior
sapience_notes.value: When adding a third no-argument-implied mode (pick) to a script whose existing contract treated '--confirm with no other mode flag' as a missing-required-argument refusal, an explicit guard for 'confirm with neither mode flag' is needed to keep that pre-existing refusal message intact -- a literal 'neither flag present -> new default mode' selector would silently reclassify that combination into the new mode instead of preserving the old refusal.
